subject: RFP: SLA measurement, burst attribution, and evidence matrix
messages:
From: Sara Hutchins <sara.hutchins@orioncorp.com>

Cc: procurement@orioncorp.com
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: Measurement methodology clarifications (SLA section)

Karthik,

Thanks for your initial RFP submission. Procurement has a few clarifying questions about the SLA measurement and crediting methodology in section 6:

1) How do you define the "availability window" for our account and how are multi-region requests attributed to that window?
2) For partial degradations (e.g., elevated tail latency on a subset of routes), do you compute credits per-route or at the account level?
3) Please provide an explicit credit calculation example for a 72-hour incident that impacted 2 of 8 production zones for 45 minutes.
4) What telemetry sources are used to drive the SLA (customer-facing request logs, internal agent telemetry, synthetic probes)? Which source is authoritative?
5) Are scheduled maintenance windows pre-excluded and how much advance notice is required?

We also need a short list of the evidence artifacts you would provide for an audit request. Ideally a CSV sample and a mapping to your measurement steps.

Can you respond by EOD Monday so procurement can close out the evaluation?

Regards,
Sara Hutchins
Sr. Procurement Manager
OrionCorp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Hutchins <sara.hutchins@orioncorp.com>, procurement@orioncorp.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: RFP: Measurement methodology clarifications (SLA section)

Sara — thank you for the clear list. Attached are: (1) Redwood_SLA_Evidence_Matrix_v1.3.pdf (walkthrough of measurement steps), and (2) sample-telemetry-csvs.zip (redacted request logs and probe results). Below is a concise summary of our approach and the worked example you asked for.

Summary (short):
- Availability window: We evaluate SLAs on rolling calendar windows aligned to the contract period (UTC). For multi-region traffic, each request is attributed to the region of the serving inference instance at the moment the request completes (region determined by final egress compute).
- Credit scope: Credits are calculated at the account level but weighted by affected route groups when degradation affects fewer than 100% of routes. This hybrid model keeps credits predictable while ensuring localized failures are not over-penalized.
- Telemetry precedence: Authoritative source is customer-facing request logs (edge request acceptance/response timestamps) instrumented by Redwood SDKs and our edge collectors. Supplementary sources: internal kernel-level traces and synthetic probe runs. When discrepancies exist, a reconciliation algorithm (described in the matrix) selects the request-log timeline unless customer-provided evidence demonstrates a persistent mismatch.
- Maintenance: Scheduled maintenance windows are pre-excluded if notified 72 hours in advance via official account contact and posted to our Status page. Emergency maintenance is treated case-by-case but we provide a post-event justification.

Worked example (72-hour incident affecting 2 of 8 zones for 45 minutes):
- Contract SLA: 99.95% monthly availability (per calendar month).
- Baseline: 30 days * 24h = 43,200 minutes in month.
- Measured downtime minutes attributable to account-level failure: 45 minutes impacting 25% of production zones for a single route-group.
- Route-weighting: Affected route-group represents 20% of monthly request volume (determined from historical routing distribution). Account-level effective outage minutes = 45 * (20%) = 9 equivalent minutes of full-account outage.
- Availability impact = (43,200 - 9) / 43,200 = 99.9792% --> above 99.95% SLA so no service credit owed.

If the same 45-minute event had impacted 100% of zones (full outage), availability impact would be 45/43,200 = 99.8969% -> falls below SLA threshold; crediting follows the contract formula: credit = min(100%, ((SLA_target - measured_availability) / SLA_target) * 100%) applied to monthly service fee. The matrix contains a worked numeric example for a $100k monthly bill.

Evidence we provide for audit:
- Customer-facing request logs (redacted) with request_id, timestamp, region, route, response_code, latency_ms.
- Internal cluster allocations and instance-level health events (time-windowed).
- Synthetic probe runbook and probe timestamps.
- Reconciliation output CSV that maps request_ids used for final measurement to probe traces and health events (example included in the zip).

Attachments in the matrix: measurement steps (enumerated), reconciliation algorithm pseudo-code, a sample calculation spreadsheet (RFP_Response_Sec6_SLA_Appendix.xlsx).

We intentionally favor request-level logs as the primary authoritative stream because they reflect customer-observed behavior; the reconciliation step prevents measurement drift from transient telemetry gaps.

I'll attach the matrix and the sample CSV now. Happy to walk through this on a short call if helpful — otherwise we can update wording and send as final to Procurement.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Reliability & Evidentiary Services
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: RFP: Measurement methodology clarifications (SLA section)

Marissa — thanks, that was fast and very helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we close:

1) For the route-weighting lookup you mentioned, will you supply the month-to-date routing distribution CSV as part of post-incident evidence?
2) For high-frequency transient spikes (sub-5-second latency bursts) that affect 10% of requests for 10 minutes, do you aggregate across the minute or second granularity for measurement?
3) If we want per-route credit visibility (rather than just an account-level number) for reporting purposes, can you expose the same credit calculation broken down by route-group?

If you can answer those three lines, we can finalize procurement scoring.

Thanks,
Sara

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Hutchins <sara.hutchins@orioncorp.com>, procurement@orioncorp.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: RFP: Measurement methodology clarifications (SLA section) — final clarifications

Sara — quick answers to close the loop:

1) Route-weighting CSV: Yes — we include the month-to-date routing distribution and the historical 90-day baseline CSV as part of the post-incident evidence pack. Those CSVs are signed/hashed and time-stamped in the evidence bundle.

2) Temporal aggregation: Measurement is done at 1-second granularity where request-level logs are available; for the final crediting calculation we align into 1-minute windows to avoid micro-noise from sub-second jitter. In your example (10% of requests for 10 minutes at sub-5-second bursts), we would compute the per-minute affected volume and then apply the route-weight to produce equivalent account outage minutes. This ensures repeatability across telemetry sources.

3) Per-route credit visibility: We can provide the credit calculation broken down by route-group as part of the evidence pack and customer-facing SLA report. Our default settlement communicates account-level credits per contract, but we include an appendix with the per-route breakdown for transparency.

Next steps: I will upload the signed evidence matrix and the sample CSVs to the Drive link we've shared and deliver a short one-hour walkthrough with your technical procurement team if you'd like. If that is acceptable, please confirm and Procurement can close scoring.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
